planning.objective: Define what to build, with what budget and in how much time, before spending on any material.
steps: List your household's needs (bedrooms, bathrooms, parking spots, common areas).
Set a realistic maximum budget, including a contingency reserve of at least 10%.
Research the land's documentation (title, zoning, maximum allowed footprint).
Set realistic deadlines per stage, considering the season and labor availability.
Gather visual references and build an inspiration folder to discuss with your designer.
mistakes: Not setting aside a contingency and running out of budget mid-project.
Ignoring municipal fees and permits in the initial budget.
Underestimating how long each stage takes out of optimism.
tips: Always start with what's non-negotiable (number of bedrooms, accessibility) before aesthetics.
Talk to people who have already built in your area to calibrate cost and time expectations.
Keep everything in one place (including this app) so you don't lose decisions already made.

design.objective: Turn the needs identified in planning into an approvable architectural design.
steps: Hire a licensed architect or engineer for the architectural design.
Validate the design against the budget set during planning.
Submit the design for approval with your local building authority, when required.
Review the final design with everyone who will live there before approving it.
mistakes: Skipping legal approval and building irregularly.
Approving a design without checking whether it fits the budget.
tips: Ask your designer for a cost-per-m² estimate as early as the design phase.
Keep every version of the design — you'll compare it against what actually gets built.
checklist: Design reviewed by everyone who will live there

siteWork.objective: Prepare the site to receive the foundation: clearing, leveling and laying out the building.
steps: Clear the site (remove vegetation, debris and topsoil).
Lay out the building (mark axes and corners per the design) using batter boards.
Level the site as needed for the chosen foundation type.
Set up temporary water and power connections for the site.
mistakes: Not removing the topsoil layer before founding.
Laying out the building without checking square (90° angles) at the corners.
tips: Check the layout with the rectangle's diagonals (both diagonals should be equal).
Photograph the site before you start — it helps with any surprise later on.

foundation.objective: Build the base that transfers the building's weight to the soil, safely and per the defined foundation type.
steps: Confirm the foundation type defined by the structural design (footing, raft, piles, etc.) — never choose it yourself without a soil study.
Excavate to the exact levels and dimensions shown in the design.
Set up the formwork and rebar per the structural design.
Install any pipe sleeves that cross the foundation before pouring concrete.
Request the responsible engineer's inspection before pouring, if applicable.
Pour in a single continuous stage whenever possible, avoiding unplanned cold joints.
Vibrate the concrete to remove air bubbles.
Cure the concrete (keep it moist) for at least the first 7 days.
Wait for the curing period before starting the structure stage.
mistakes: Choosing the foundation type without a soil study and structural design.
Pouring without checking plumb, level and square of the formwork.
Not curing the concrete properly, compromising final strength.
Forgetting pipe sleeves and later breaking the finished foundation to add them.
tips: Always request the invoice and mix design if you buy ready-mix concrete.
Photograph the rebar before pouring — it's the only way to check it later.
Never start the foundation without a structural design signed by a licensed professional.
Consider the water table level — it may require additional waterproofing.
checklist: Structural design in hand and approved by a licensed professional

structure.objective: Build the columns and beams that support the slabs and roof, per the structural design.
steps: Set up formwork for columns and beams per the structural design.
Install the rebar sized by the responsible engineer.
Pour columns and beams, vibrating to remove air bubbles.
Respect the curing and formwork-removal schedule set by the responsible engineer before continuing.
mistakes: Removing formwork before the minimum curing period.
Changing column position or size without the engineer's approval.
tips: Never cut or bend rebar on site without authorization from the responsible engineer.
Shoring must stay in place until formally released by the responsible professional.
checklist: Formwork and rebar checked before pouring

masonry.objective: Build the infill walls, plumb and level, following the design's layout.
steps: Mark the position of every wall on the floor with a tape measure and square.
Lay the first course with extra care — it defines the rest of the wall.
Use a mason's line stretched between corners as a level guide for each course.
Check the wall's plumb every 3-4 courses with a spirit level.
Leave openings for doors and windows per the frame design's measurements.
Install lintels above every door and window opening.
Fill vertical and horizontal joints evenly with mortar.
Wait for the mortar to cure before starting wall coverings over it.
mistakes: Not checking plumb every few courses — the error only shows up (and is expensive to fix) at the top of the wall.
Forgetting lintels over doors/windows, causing cracks later.
Using broken blocks at corners, weakening the bond.
Laying on top of an out-of-square first course.
tips: Lightly wet ceramic blocks before laying — it keeps them from pulling water out of the mortar too fast.
Use this app's masonry calculator so you don't buy too much or too little material.
Always keep a waste margin (10% is this calculator's default, adjustable).

slabs.objective: Build the slab that separates floors or closes the roof, per the structural design.
steps: Set up shoring and formwork for the slab per the design.
Install the rebar (top/bottom) and any embedded services shown in the design.
Pour the slab in one continuous stage, vibrating properly.
Cure the slab and respect the shoring-removal schedule set by the responsible engineer.
mistakes: Removing shoring before the recommended technical schedule.
Forgetting to embed conduits/pipes before pouring.
tips: Never overload the slab (stacked materials) before it fully cures.
Confirm the shoring schedule per floor with the responsible engineer.

roofing.objective: Close up the building with the roof, ensuring watertightness and correct water drainage.
steps: Confirm the minimum recommended pitch for the chosen tile type against the design.
Build the structure (wood or metal) per the roof design.
Install the underlayment/membrane, when specified, before the tiles.
Fix tiles from bottom to top, respecting the manufacturer's minimum overlap.
Install ridge caps at the water meeting points.
Install flashing where the roof meets walls and chimneys to prevent leaks.
Install gutters and downspouts.
Do a watertightness inspection simulating rain before releasing the ceiling below.
mistakes: Using a pitch lower than the tile manufacturer's minimum recommendation.
Not installing flashing where the roof meets walls.
Working at height without a safety harness/lifeline.
Undersizing gutters for the region's rainfall volume.
tips: Roof work is work at height — always use fall-protection equipment.
Prefer dry, low-wind days for assembly.
Keep a small reserve of tiles from the same batch for future repairs (color can vary between batches).
checklist: Height PPE used throughout the stage

waterproofing.objective: Prevent water intrusion in critical areas (bathrooms, exposed slabs, outdoor areas, pools).
steps: Identify every area that needs waterproofing (wet areas, exposed slabs, planters).
Prepare the surface: clean, dust-free, cracks sealed.
Apply the waterproofing system per the manufacturer's spec (number of coats, cure time between them).
Do a watertightness test (ponding water for 72h) before covering it with finishes.
mistakes: Covering the waterproofing with finishes before it's fully cured.
Not extending waterproofing up the walls (waterproof skirting) in wet areas.
Skipping the watertightness test before closing the area with flooring.
tips: Photograph the waterproofing before covering it — you won't be able to see it again.
Keep the product's technical data sheet — useful for future maintenance.

frames.objective: Install doors and windows in the openings left by the masonry.
steps: Check the opening's measurements against the frame before installing.
Position the frame plumb and level, temporarily shimming it.
Fix the frame per the manufacturer's method (screws, sub-frame, expanding foam).
Seal around it to prevent leaks and unwanted air infiltration.
mistakes: Installing out of plumb, making it hard to close properly later.
Not sealing around the frame properly.
tips: Measure the opening at three points (bottom, middle, top) — masonry is rarely perfectly straight.
Protect aluminum/wood frames with plastic film for the rest of the project.

hydraulic.objective: Install water supply and drain piping before walls and floors are closed.
steps: Mark the route of every pipe run on walls/floor per the plumbing design.
Chase the walls (shallow chases that don't compromise structure) to embed pipes.
Assemble the cold/hot water piping with the correct fittings.
Assemble the drain piping with the minimum slope needed for gravity flow.
Install shut-off valves in accessible locations for future maintenance.
Pressure-test the water piping before closing the walls.
Flow-test the drain piping before closing.
Only close (chases, subfloor) after both tests pass.
mistakes: Closing the wall before testing the piping — leaks stay hidden and are expensive to fix.
Insufficient slope on drain piping, causing recurring clogs.
Chasing too deep into structural walls, compromising strength.
Mixing potable water piping with reuse water without clear labeling.
tips: Photograph all the piping before closing it up — a gold-standard map for future maintenance.
Centralize water shut-off valves in one easily accessible spot (e.g., laundry area).
Use this app's plumbing calculator only as a shopping-list estimate — the actual routing comes from the design.
checklist: Drains assembled with slope and flow-tested
Shut-off valves in an accessible spot

sanitary.objective: Finish fixtures, fittings and sanitary connections after floors and walls are closed.
steps: Confirm the drain piping was tested during the plumbing stage.
Install the toilet, sink and other fixtures per the design's measurements.
Connect fittings (faucets, finish valves, showers).
Test the whole assembly (flush, drainage, no leaks) before considering it done.
mistakes: Installing fixtures before the grout/sealant has cured.
Not testing the whole assembly before releasing the room for use.
tips: Use sanitary silicone (with fungicide) at the base of toilets and sinks.
Keep the manual for each fixture/fitting — it helps with future maintenance.

electrical.objective: Install the entire electrical infrastructure safely, from the distribution panel to every outlet.
steps: Confirm the electrical design sized by a licensed professional (never improvise the electrical installation).
Mark the position of every point (outlets, switches, light fixtures) on the walls.
Chase shallow channels to embed conduits per the design.
Run conduits, then cables, keeping circuits separated per the design.
Install the distribution panel with breakers, RCD and surge protection sized by the professional.
Install the grounding system — a non-negotiable safety item.
Connect outlets, switches and light points, testing each circuit's continuity.
Do a full energization test with the responsible professional present.
Only close walls/ceiling after the whole installation is technically approved.
mistakes: Sizing the installation without a licensed professional — fire and shock risk.
Skipping grounding or RCD protection, compromising the whole house's safety.
Mixing wiring from different circuits in the same conduit without need.
Closing walls before the full energization test.
tips: Use standardized cable colors (live, neutral, ground) — it helps future maintenance.
Label the distribution panel indicating what each breaker controls.
Never skip the licensed professional — this is a mandatory safety item, not optional.
checklist: Electrical design from a licensed professional in hand
Conduits and cables installed per design
Panel with RCD and surge protection installed
Energization test approved by the professional

network.objective: Install wired network (Ethernet) infrastructure for stable internet throughout the house.
steps: Define the network points (TVs, office, router, cameras) in the design.
Run network cables alongside electrical conduits (in separate conduits from power cabling).
Install the rack/patch panel in a central, ventilated location.
Test every point with a cable tester before closing walls.
mistakes: Running network cable inside the same conduit as power cabling (interference).
Not testing the points before closing the wall.
tips: Cat6 cable already handles current and near-future speeds well — worth the investment.
Centralize network equipment in a ventilated rack, away from heat sources.

telephony.objective: Install basic landline telephony infrastructure, when applicable.
steps: Define the telephony points you actually need (often replaced today by VoIP/mobile).
Run the wiring alongside the network cabling, in its own conduit.
Test the line at each point before closing the wall.
mistakes: Investing in many traditional landline points without checking if they'll still be used.
tips: Consider adding more network/Wi-Fi points instead of traditional landline points.

hvac.objective: Prepare the infrastructure for air conditioning and ventilation before finishes.
steps: Define unit positions and the refrigerant line/drain route.
Leave dedicated electrical points for each unit, sized by the electrician.
Plan the correct drain line slope to avoid indoor leaks.
mistakes: Not planning a dedicated electrical point, overloading an existing circuit.
Drain line without proper slope, causing indoor leaks.
tips: Assess each room's solar orientation before sizing unit capacity.
Keep piping accessible for future maintenance.

solarPower.objective: Install a photovoltaic system for power generation, always with professional design and installation.
steps: Use this app's solar calculator to estimate an initial system size.
Hire a professional feasibility assessment (roof structure, orientation, shading).
Formalize the electrical design and the grid connection request with your utility.
Oversee the professional installation of panels, inverter and dedicated electrical protection.
mistakes: Sizing and installing without a professional structural and shading assessment.
Not registering the system with your power utility.
tips: Solar panels perform better with shading assessed hour-by-hour, not just 'gets direct sun'.
Keep all equipment warranty documentation.
checklist: Grid connection request submitted to the utility

solarHeating.objective: Install a solar water heating system, reducing the electric/gas load of showers and taps.
steps: Use this app's solar heating calculator to estimate collectors and tank size.
Position collectors with good solar orientation and the manufacturer's recommended tilt.
Install the storage tank and a backup system (electric or gas) for sunless days.
Test the full system before considering it done.
mistakes: Installing collectors with partial shading during part of the day.
Not planning a backup system for cloudy days.
tips: Thermal insulation on the piping significantly improves system efficiency.

flooring.objective: Install the final flooring with correct leveling, layout and finish.
steps: Confirm the subfloor is level, cured and clean before starting.
Define the layout (direction and starting point) facing the room's main door.
Choose the mortar suited to the flooring type and substrate.
Apply mortar with a notched trowel, in the right amount to avoid voids.
Lay the tiles respecting the joint spacers defined in the design.
Cut edge pieces with the right tool, avoiding chips.
Wait for the mortar's cure time before grouting (usually 24 to 72h).
Apply grout, filling joints well, removing excess while still fresh.
Clean the floor, removing grout residue with a damp cloth.
Do a final inspection: hollow sound (loose tile), leveling between tiles, and cleanliness.
mistakes: Laying tile over an uncured or unlevel subfloor.
Applying too little mortar, leaving voids that crack the tile later (hollow sound).
Not respecting expansion joints in large or outdoor areas.
Grouting before the mortar has cured.
tips: Always open boxes from different batches and mix them together — avoids shade mismatches.
Use this app's flooring calculator to know how many boxes to buy (it already rounds up).
Keep extra tiles from each batch for future repairs.
checklist: No hollow sound found after laying

wallCovering.objective: Apply wall coverings (ceramic, porcelain, texture) in wet areas or feature areas.
steps: Confirm waterproofing (when applicable) has already been tested.
Mark the layout starting from the room's most visible point.
Apply mortar and lay tiles plumb and level.
Grout after the mortar's cure time.
mistakes: Tiling over untested waterproofing.
Not checking plumb, resulting in visibly crooked grout lines.
tips: Wet areas benefit from tiling up to the ceiling, or at least 1.5m above the water point.

drywall.objective: Build walls and ceilings with drywall, a dry construction system.
steps: Mark the position of the metal frame (tracks and studs) on floor and ceiling.
Install the metal frame level and plumb.
Run any planned electrical/plumbing services before closing the panels.
Screw drywall panels to the frame, taping and mudding the joints.
mistakes: Closing the panels before running all planned services.
Not treating joints properly, leaving visible marks after painting.
tips: Use moisture-resistant (green) boards in wet areas.
Reinforce fixing points for cabinets/TVs with extra blocking.

painting.objective: Apply the final paint, protecting and finishing surfaces.
steps: Protect floors, frames and furniture with drop cloths/tape before starting.
Sand the surface to remove imperfections and improve paint adhesion.
Remove sanding dust with a damp cloth before applying any product.
Apply spackle to imperfections when needed, and sand again once dry.
Apply primer/sealer, respecting the manufacturer's drying time.
Dilute the paint per the manufacturer's instructions, when applicable.
Apply the first coat, cutting in corners with a brush and rolling large areas.
Respect the recoat interval on the label before applying the second coat.
Apply the second coat (or more, for the desired coverage).
Remove protection only once the paint is fully dry to the touch.
mistakes: Painting over a dusty surface or one with residual moisture.
Not respecting the manufacturer's recoat interval.
Diluting the paint beyond what's recommended, losing coverage and durability.
Not protecting floors and frames, causing splatters that are hard to remove.
tips: Use this app's paint calculator to know how many liters to buy based on coverage.
Buy paint from the same batch for the whole room — avoids subtle shade differences.
Well-ventilated rooms speed up drying and reduce odor.
checklist: Coats applied respecting the manufacturer's interval

doors.objective: Install interior and exterior doors, hinges and locks.
steps: Check the opening and frame alignment before hanging the door.
Install hinges aligned and level.
Install the lock, testing it before considering it done.
Adjust clearances for smooth opening/closing.
mistakes: Installing the door before the frame's final paint has dried.
Not testing the lock before releasing the room.
tips: Doors in wet areas benefit from a small extra bottom gap for ventilation.

deck.objective: Build a wood or composite deck on a prepared base.
steps: Prepare the base (level, drained) where the deck will sit.
Use this app's deck calculator to estimate boards, joists and screws.
Install support joists at the defined spacing, level with each other.
Treat/protect the wood before assembly, if not already factory-treated.
Fix boards with the manufacturer's recommended expansion gap.
Leave a small gap between the deck and walls for ventilation.
Apply the final protective finish (varnish, oil) suited to the chosen material.
Reapply the protective finish periodically per the recommended maintenance schedule.
mistakes: Resting the deck directly on undrained soil, encouraging rot.
Not leaving an expansion gap between boards.
Ignoring the need to periodically reapply the protective finish.
tips: Composite (WPC) wood needs less maintenance than solid wood, but costs more.
Ventilation underneath the deck is essential for its durability.

pool.objective: Plan and build a pool with structural, plumbing and electrical safety.
steps: Choose the pool type (masonry, vinyl liner, fiberglass) with a professional's help.
Get a dedicated structural design — a pool is a structure holding a large water load.
Execute the plumbing (recirculation, filtration) per the manufacturer's/installer's design.
Execute the electrical work (pump, lighting) always with dedicated RCD protection and a licensed professional.
Do a watertightness test before applying the final finish.
mistakes: Building without a dedicated structural design for the pool.
Connecting the pump/lighting without dedicated RCD protection.
Skipping the watertightness test before the final finish.
tips: A pool on a deck or slab needs its own structural check — use this app's weight-estimate module only as a starting reference, never as a safety approval.
checklist: Electrical with dedicated RCD installed by a professional

jacuzzi.objective: Install a hot tub/spa with structural, electrical and plumbing safety.
steps: Confirm the base (deck/slab) supports the full weight when filled — always with a professional assessment.
Provide a dedicated electrical point with RCD protection, installed by a licensed electrician.
Install the plumbing (fill, drain) per the manufacturer's manual.
Test the heating and jet system before use.
mistakes: Not assessing the support structure for the full weight of water and people.
Connecting the unit without a dedicated circuit and RCD protection.
tips: Check the manufacturer's warranty and recommended maintenance before installing.
checklist: Support structure assessed by a professional
Dedicated electrical circuit with RCD installed

outdoorArea.objective: Build flooring, light roofing and infrastructure for the outdoor area.
steps: Choose a suitable outdoor floor finish (slip-resistant, weather-resistant).
Plan slope for rainwater drainage.
Install outdoor electrical points with proper protection for wet areas (IP65 or higher).
mistakes: Using indoor (non-slip-resistant) flooring in a wet outdoor area.
tips: Outdoor outlets should have splash-proof covers.

landscaping.objective: Finish gardens, lawns and landscaping elements.
steps: Prepare the soil (fertilizing, leveling) before planting.
Choose species suited to the local climate and sun exposure of each area.
Install an irrigation system, if applicable, before final planting.
mistakes: Planting species unsuited to the local climate, creating excessive maintenance.
tips: Native species generally need less maintenance and water.
checklist: Species chosen to match local climate

finishes.objective: Handle the final finishing details before project handover.
steps: Do final paint touch-ups and any pending spot repairs.
Install final fixtures (mirrors, hardware, shelves).
Do a detailed post-construction cleaning of every room.
mistakes: Doing the final cleaning before finishing all pending small repairs.
tips: Inspect with good lighting (including a raking flashlight) to spot small paint imperfections.

finalInspection.objective: Review the entire project before considering it complete, including safety aspects.
steps: Walk through the project with every stage's checklist marked complete.
Test every electrical installation (outlets, breakers, RCD) one last time.
Test every plumbing installation (valves, drains, leaks) one last time.
Check doors, windows and locks.
Gather all technical documentation (designs, invoices, warranties) in one place.
mistakes: Not keeping technical documentation organized — it hinders future maintenance and any eventual sale.
Skipping the final electrical and plumbing safety test.
tips: Export this app's backup (the full project) and keep it with the project's physical documentation.
Photograph the final state of every room for future reference.
